note: THE CHECKER RECOVERS ABOUT A QUARTER OF THE CYNGHANEDD THAT IS THERE. Nothing was tuned; the shortfall is the finding. Three mechanical causes, each with a minimal repro. DEFECT 1, INTERNAL APOSTROPHE: units() strips only leading/trailing quotes, so the elisions Welsh uses constantly are out of inventory — units("a'i") is None, units("ai") is ['a','i']; units("sy'n") is None, units("syn") is ['s','y','n']. skeleton() then returns None and the WHOLE LINE is 'unreadable' before any rule runs. 31.0% of the Alun corpus contains one. DEFECT 2, PRINTED COMMAS READ AS CAESURAS: cynghanedd() splits on [,/|], so ordinary verse punctuation is taken for the gwant and a 3-comma line is forced down the sain path — 'Eto, Aled, atolwg' is REFUSED ('sain needs rhyme AND alliteration'), while 'Eto Aled | atolwg' returns croes on skeleton ['t']. DEFECT 3, THE GWANT IS PRINTED AS '--' AND '--' IS NOT IN THE SPLIT SET: this transcription does mark the englyn gwant, with a dash, e.g. 'Bryd a chorff yn ddiorffwys,--'; the comma split leaves a half of '--' whose words all strip to empty, so skeleton() returns None and the line is 'unreadable'. 14.6% of lines carry a '--'.
